audit_findings.title: Post-anchor acquisition debt has no matching interest cost in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $303.8 million annualized pre-tax incremental interest: $220.2 million on the May 2026 notes at filed effective rates plus $83.6 million on $2.1 billion of commercial paper at 3.98%; equal to 20.5% of the $1,481.3 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE retains interest expense, but FY2025 OE contains only $23 million of pre-acquisition interest while the bridge uses $7.517 billion of June 2026 debt.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate cash flows generated from operations, cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and long-term marketable securities will be sufficient to meet our liquidity needs for at least the next 12 months, although we do expect to seek additional debt financing to fund our acquisition of Armis Security Ltd. discussed in Note 5 “Business Combinations” in the notes to our consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch, not merely a possibility. The omitted annualized financing cost is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially lowering operating value, although the after-tax effect requires a coherent pro forma tax calculation.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate OE with the post-close debt's annual interest, issuance fees and taxes, together with Armis and Veza OE and integration costs, all measured on the same post-close basis.

audit_findings.title: Armis is incorrectly described as contributing a partial FY2025 year
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.637 billion filed purchase consideration, equal to 27.7% of the $27.549 billion base equity value; acquired OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation capitalizes pre-close FY2025 OE while using a June 2026 bridge containing the acquisition's cash depletion, debt and acquired assets and liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Armis Security Ltd. a cyber-exposure management and cyber-physical security solutions provider, for approximately $ 7.75 billion cash consideration, subject to customary adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The error is demonstrated: Armis closed April 20, 2026, after FY2025 ended, so it contributed no FY2025 operations. The omitted acquired earning power could raise value, while financing, integration and maintenance requirements lower it. At 27.7% of modeled base equity value, the perimeter mismatch is material even though its net direction cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Replace the incorrect perimeter note and rerun either entirely on December 2025 pre-close figures or on a post-close basis containing normalized Armis OE, integration costs, maintenance investment, taxes and financing expense.

audit_findings.title: Veza may be a second omitted post-anchor perimeter change
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.237 billion filed purchase consideration, equal to 4.5% of the $27.549 billion base equity value; acquired OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Veza's March 2, 2026 closing affects the June bridge, while no Veza operations, financing effects or integration economics are present in FY2025 anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Veza Technologies, Inc., a privately held company that provides a unified access platform, with native products offering access search, access intelligence, access monitoring and access workflows, for approximately $ 1.25 billion cash consideration, subject to customary adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The closing is now demonstrated rather than hypothetical, but the record does not quantify Veza's normalized OE or incremental costs. Its transaction size establishes a potentially meaningful mismatch but does not establish that the net valuation effect is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Veza's cash funding and assumed liabilities to the June bridge, obtain standalone or pro forma OE and integration costs, and rerun it on the same post-close basis as Armis.

audit_findings.title: Moveworks shares represent a claim on an anchor containing only days of its earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately 9.6 million acquisition shares, or 0.88% of 1,092.189 million fully diluted shares; $2.407 billion purchase consideration, equal to 8.7% of base equity value; normalized acquired OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The fully diluted denominator includes the Moveworks acquisition shares, while FY2025 OE includes operations only from the December 15 closing through year-end.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 15, 2025, we acquired all outstanding shares of Moveworks, Inc. (“Moveworks”), a privately held company that provides enterprise search and front-end virtual agent technology.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but its net value effect cannot be established without Moveworks' normalized OE. The acquisition shares alone reduce per-share value by less than 1%; the potentially larger numerator effect remains unquantified and could be positive or negative after integration and maintenance costs.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Moveworks standalone or pro forma revenue, operating costs, integration costs, taxes and maintenance investment, then rerun a normalized combined-company OE anchor without removing the acquisition shares.

audit_findings.title: Large fixed cloud commitments may not be absorbed by mechanical OE growth
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $4.902 billion of filed remaining payments through 2030, including approximately $2.9 billion in 2030; incremental unabsorbed burden unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cloud expense already incurred is embedded in OE, but future minimum payments could depress OE and growth if committed capacity costs exceed the revenue or efficiency benefits generated.
audit_findings.evidence: We have entered into various non-cancellable agreements with cloud service providers, under which we have committed to spend an aggregate of approximately $ 4.8 billion through 2030 on cloud services.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking utilization risk rather than a demonstrated omission. Payment timing may differ from consumption, and the record does not separate already-modeled operating expense from incremental unused capacity. It should therefore be monitored rather than deducted wholesale.
audit_findings.action: Map the annual commitments against cloud expense embedded in FY2025 and 2026 results, contracted utilization, revenue capacity and scenario growth; rerun only the incremental unabsorbed portion.

audit_findings.title: Private strategic investments are added without an evident valuation haircut
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum direct bridge downside of $2.073 billion, or $1.90 per share and 7.5% of the $27.549 billion base equity value; a zero valuation would reduce base value from $25.22 to approximately $23.33 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the carrying amount of predominantly non-marketable Level 3 strategic investments dollar for dollar to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: All of our strategic investments in privately held companies are subject to a risk of partial or total loss of invested capital.
audit_findings.explanation: A realization haircut is warranted for analytical quality, but even the extreme assumption that all stakes are worthless would leave intrinsic value far below the $145.59 market price and would not change the valuation conclusion. The latest carrying amount also includes $360 million of first-half 2026 net upward adjustments, underscoring valuation uncertainty without increasing the maximum bridge exposure beyond $2.073 billion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each holding's security rights, observable financings, impairment indicators, taxes and liquidity restrictions; apply realization values in the next rerun, while noting that the full write-off sensitivity does not alter the present conclusion.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed/computed residuals of $49.6 million to $105.0 million annually for FY2019-FY2024; FY2025 residual unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible D&A not identified separately remains an expense in OE; any portion proven non-economic would be added back to OE and capitalized.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $49.6m (19.7% of filed D&A); FY2020 $65.4m (19.4% of filed D&A); FY2021 $84.0m (17.8% of filed D&A); FY2022 $91.0m (21.0% of filed D&A); FY2023 $105.0m (18.7% of filed D&A); FY2024 $99.0m (17.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated overstatement exists because the treatment is conservative.
